protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Verified. Attacker-controlled shared-library SCM content is copied or archived without rejecting symbolic links; the external-library global-variable help path then reads a vars/*.txt entry, while the later libraryResource canonical-path check covered only resources. Commit 5cc688825312c805c93cadd0b61c42cdbf45f61f fixes the common retrieval boundary by rejecting symlinks and non-regular files before and after retrieval and before cached copies.

The first atomic commit connecting external-library vars.jar entries to UserDefinedGlobalVariable help URLs is 4c912007ecc11d1fd72626e88bedd7c3afabeab5.

findings: CVE.org reports CVE-2026-48921 as PUBLISHED under the Jenkins CNA, with versions through 797.v90ea_a_9b_e45a_0 affected; the Jenkins advisory names 798.v5cc688825312 as fixed. The advisory is not a false positive.

The primary record conflates the first external SCM loader with the first complete vulnerability chain. At 62281a93828713fec238c29f34bdee420ac5c03a, external-library global variables and their help URLs are not yet registered; commit 4c912007ecc11d1fd72626e88bedd7c3afabeab5 first adds that registration and help read path while retaining unvalidated vars.jar packaging.

Later commits, including ce623b82d6453a96f0f0bc05959d2e76c7b61a0c, e8a10e89da492ab53c6d757da736e50d886f5d39, and 76ad53e052aa7b9a7d0101b23e83a8ed5ab43feb, change storage or move the same retrieval path and are not the first complete source-to-sink commit.
The corrected BIC has the same human author identity and no AI marker, so the primary NOT_AI verdict does not change.
